name: Google Quantum AI
short_summary: Google Quantum AI (founded 2012, Santa Barbara CA) is Alphabet's superconducting quantum computing division. It achieved quantum supremacy with the 53-qubit Sycamore processor in 2019, demonstrated below-threshold quantum error correction with the 105-qubit Willow chip in December 2024, and claimed verifiable quantum advantage with the Quantum Echoes algorithm in October 2025. The division operates its own qubit fabrication facility and publishes the open-source Cirq framework, pursuing a five-milestone roadmap toward commercially useful error-corrected quantum computation by 2029.

name: IBM Quantum
short_summary: IBM Quantum (est. 2016, Yorktown Heights NY) is IBM's quantum computing division operating the world's first public cloud quantum service (IBM Quantum Experience, 2016) and the largest fleet of superconducting processors. Its hardware roadmap progressed from 127-qubit Eagle (2021) through 433-qubit Osprey (2022) to 1,121-qubit Condor and 133-qubit Heron (2023), with Heron powering the modular IBM Quantum System Two. The division also publishes Qiskit, the most widely used open-source quantum SDK. IBM targets 200-qubit / 100 M-gate Starling by 2029 and a 2,000-qubit / 1 B-gate Blue Jay system by 2033.

differentiators: First to offer cloud-accessible quantum computing to the public (IBM Quantum Experience, May 2016), democratising access to quantum hardware worldwide
Largest open-source quantum software ecosystem via Qiskit — over 6 million installs and 300,000 installations per month as of 2025
Demonstrated evidence for quantum utility on a 127-qubit Eagle processor in Nature (June 2023), executing circuits beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation
IBM Quantum System Two (Yorktown Heights, 2023) is the industry's first modular quantum computer, housing three Heron processors with a shared cryogenic infrastructure
Publicly committed roadmap to quantum-centric supercomputing extending to 2033 (Starling 200-qubit / 100 M gates by 2029; Blue Jay 2,000-qubit / 1 B gates by 2033)

milestones.claim: IBM launched IBM Quantum Experience — the first cloud-based service giving the public hands-on access to a real quantum processor (5 superconducting qubits) hosted at the T.J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights.

Released Qiskit (Quantum Information Software Kit) as an open-source Python SDK, the first publicly available quantum software development kit, enabling users to build and run quantum circuits on IBM hardware and simulators.

Launched the IBM Q Network — an ecosystem of Fortune 500 companies, academic institutions, and national labs (initial 12 members including JPMorgan Chase, Daimler, Samsung, Barclays, Oak Ridge National Lab, University of Oxford) with early commercial access to IBM Q systems.

Unveiled IBM Q System One at CES 2019 — the world's first integrated commercial quantum computing system, housing a 20-qubit processor in a 9-foot borosilicate glass enclosure designed for continuous operation outside a research lab.

Achieved Quantum Volume 64 on a 27-qubit system — doubling the previous record of QV 32 — through a combination of dynamical decoupling, compiler optimisations, shorter two-qubit gates, and excited-state promoted readout.

Unveiled Eagle — IBM's first 127-qubit quantum processor and the first quantum chip whose state space cannot be reliably represented by a classical computer — at the IBM Quantum Summit 2021. Eagle introduced a multi-level wiring heavy-hexagonal lattice to minimise qubit crosstalk.

Unveiled Osprey — a 433-qubit processor with more than three times the qubits of Eagle — at the IBM Quantum Summit 2022, alongside details of next-generation IBM Quantum System Two architecture for quantum-centric supercomputing.

Published "Evidence for the utility of quantum computing before fault tolerance" in Nature — demonstrating that a 127-qubit Eagle processor could compute expectation values for a 2D Ising model at circuit depths beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation.

Unveiled Condor (1,121-qubit, world's first quantum processor to exceed 1,000 qubits) and Heron (133-qubit, 3–5x improvement in error performance over Eagle with tunable couplers), and announced IBM Quantum System Two — the first modular quantum computer — operational at Yorktown Heights with three Heron processors.

name: Oxford Quantum Circuits
short_summary: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC; founded 2017, Reading, UK) is a University of Oxford spin-out that builds and operates superconducting quantum computers for cloud delivery under a Quantum-Compute-as-a-Service model. Its patented Coaxmon architecture places qubit control on the reverse face of a sapphire substrate, enabling compact, low-crosstalk scaling. OQC was the first European quantum processor on Amazon Braket (Lucy, 2022), launched the 32-qubit Toshiko enterprise platform in 2023 alongside a $100 M Series B led by SBI Investment, and deployed its GENESIS logical-era system in a New York City data centre with NVIDIA in September 2025.

differentiators: Coaxmon architecture places qubits and control wiring on opposite sides of a sapphire substrate via a through-substrate via, eliminating in-plane wiring crowding and reducing cross-talk at scale
First European quantum company on Amazon Braket (February 2022, Lucy) and first to deploy quantum computers directly into commercial data centres worldwide

Dual-rail Dimon qubit technology achieves error suppression and detection at the individual physical-qubit level, targeting a ~10x reduction in the physical-to-logical qubit overhead versus conventional surface codes
OQC GENESIS (2025) is the first quantum computer deployed inside a New York City data centre, integrated with NVIDIA Grace Hopper Superchips for hybrid quantum-AI workloads

name: Rigetti Computing
short_summary: Rigetti Computing (founded 2013, Berkeley CA; NASDAQ: RGTI) is a publicly traded superconducting quantum computing company that designs and fabricates its own processors at its Fab-1 facility in Fremont and delivers them via Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) and cloud marketplaces. It pioneered the Quil quantum instruction language and the Forest open-source SDK, went public via SPAC in March 2022, and has advanced through Aspen and Ankaa processor generations to the 108-qubit Cepheus-1 system (April 2026, 99.1% two-qubit CZ fidelity). In May 2026, Rigetti signed a letter of intent for up to $100 million in CHIPS Act funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce.

differentiators: Only quantum computing company to own and operate a dedicated in-house quantum chip fabrication facility (Fab-1, Fremont CA), enabling rapid design-to-chip cycles of approximately two weeks
Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) delivers sub-millisecond classical-quantum latency, enabling hybrid quantum-classical workloads at speed
Cepheus-1-108Q (April 2026) achieves 99.9% single-qubit and 99.1% two-qubit CZ gate fidelity, marking a significant step toward fault-tolerant thresholds
Proprietary chiplet-based multi-die architecture (introduced Aspen-M, 2022) provides a credible scaling path to 1,000+ qubits without requiring a single larger die
Quil / PyQuil / Quilc open-source software stack enables pulse-level control via Quil-T, differentiating QCS from gate-only cloud services

Launched Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) — the industry's first quantum-first cloud computing platform — offering sub-millisecond classical-quantum latency and direct access to Rigetti processors.
Rigetti processors became available on Amazon Braket as a launch partner, extending cloud access to AWS customers.

Announced a SPAC merger with Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II, Ltd. at an implied enterprise value of approximately $1.5 billion, with $261.75 million in gross proceeds (including a $147.51 million PIPE).

Completed business combination with Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II and began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under ticker RGTI, becoming one of the first standalone quantum hardware companies to list publicly via a SPAC.

Deployed Aspen-M-3 — an 80-qubit multi-chip processor built from two 40-qubit dies using Rigetti's proprietary modular chiplet architecture — to Amazon Braket, demonstrating the first commercial multi-chip superconducting quantum computer.
Chad Rigetti departed as CEO and board member; Dr. Subodh Kulkarni appointed President and CEO effective December 12, 2022, following a restructuring of the executive team after the SPAC listing.
Announced a restructuring that reduced headcount by 28% and refocused the company on near-term quantum advantage; strategy shifted to prioritise Ankaa-series processors and the QCS platform.

Launched Ankaa-1 — an 84-qubit single-chip processor using a square lattice and tunable couplers with 2x faster gates than the Aspen series — achieving 96-97% median two-qubit fidelity and targeting a path to narrow quantum advantage.
Deployed Ankaa-2 (84 qubits, 99.9% single-qubit, 98% two-qubit fidelity) to QCS and Amazon Braket, making it the highest qubit-count gate-based QPU on Braket at that time.

Completed deployment of a 24-qubit Aspen-class quantum computer at the UK National Quantum Computing Centre (NQCC) under a £10 million Innovate UK consortium with Oxford Instruments, University of Edinburgh, Phasecraft, and Standard Chartered Bank — Rigetti's first international on-premises quantum system.
Launched Ankaa-3 — an 84-qubit processor achieving 99.5% median two-qubit fSim gate fidelity and 99.0% iSWAP fidelity, the best published two-qubit performance for any Rigetti device to date.

Deployed Cepheus-1-36Q — a 36-qubit chiplet-based processor with 99.9% single-qubit and 99.5% two-qubit CZ fidelity — as the first system in the Cepheus generation, which is designed to scale to 108 qubits and beyond via multi-die assembly.

Received an $8.4 million purchase order from India's Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) to deliver a 108-qubit Cepheus-1 quantum computer for on-premises installation at C-DAC's Bengaluru centre — Rigetti's first contract for a system sale to a national computing institution.

Launched Cepheus-1-108Q (108 qubits, 99.9% single-qubit fidelity, 99.1% two-qubit CZ fidelity) for general availability on QCS and Amazon Braket — Rigetti's highest-qubit, highest-fidelity system to date.

Signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for an award of up to $100 million over three years under the CHIPS and Science Act to accelerate next-generation superconducting quantum computing R&D; the Department of Commerce will receive an equity stake in exchange.

name: Quantum Brilliance
short_summary: Quantum Brilliance (founded 2019, Canberra, Australia) is an Australian National University spin-out that develops room-temperature diamond quantum accelerators based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in synthetic diamond. Its compact, 19-inch rack-mountable QPUs — the QB-QDK series — eliminate cryogenic infrastructure, targeting HPC integration and edge quantum computing. Key milestones include the world's first on-premises room-temperature quantum computer at Pawsey Supercomputing Centre (June 2022), deployments at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (September 2025) and Fraunhofer IAF (May 2025), a Cyberagentur contract with ParityQC to build the world's first mobile quantum computer by 2027, and a Series A totalling over USD $46 million. Co-founder Marcus Doherty (119-marcus-w-doherty) is one of the world's leading NV-center theorists.

differentiators: Only commercial quantum computing platform that operates at room temperature and atmospheric pressure using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in synthetic diamond, eliminating the need for dilution refrigerators, vacuum systems, or cryogenics

Smart Diamond architecture integrates NV qubits with electronic, magnetic, and optical interfaces in a 19-inch rack-mountable form factor, enabling deployment in standard data centres, HPC facilities, and edge environments

Vertically integrated technology stack spanning diamond materials growth, device fabrication, quantum control electronics, and software, with Australia's first quantum diamond foundry under development

Targets edge quantum computing use cases (satellites, vehicles, field deployments) where cryogenic systems are impractical — a differentiated market segment not addressed by superconducting or trapped-ion platforms
approach.elevator_pitch: Quantum Brilliance develops room-temperature diamond quantum accelerators based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in synthetic diamond, enabling compact, rack-mountable QPUs that integrate directly into HPC, data centre, and edge computing environments without cryogenic infrastructure.

products.description: First-generation 2-qubit room-temperature quantum accelerator based on NV centers in synthetic diamond. Rack-mountable form factor deployable in standard data centres without cryogenic infrastructure. First deployed at Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre in June 2022.

products.description: Second-generation room-temperature quantum accelerator featuring NV centers in synthetic diamond in a standard 19-inch server rack form factor. First commercially purchased by Fraunhofer IAF (May 2025) and deployed in clusters of three parallelized QPUs at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (September 2025).

milestones.claim: Quantum Brilliance founded in Canberra as a spin-out from the Australian National University's diamond quantum science research group, co-founded by Andrew Horsley, Marcus Doherty, and Mark Luo.

Raised USD $9.7 million seed round co-led by Main Sequence and the QxBranch founders' consortium, with participation from CP Ventures, Investible, Jelix Ventures, MA Financial Group Venture Fund, R3I Ventures, and Ultratech Capital, to advance diamond quantum accelerator development and deployment.

Installed the world's first room-temperature diamond-based quantum accelerator at Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre in Perth, integrating a 2-qubit NV-center QPU with the HPE Cray EX Setonix supercomputer for hybrid quantum-classical workflows.

Established the Research Hub for Diamond Quantum Materials jointly with La Trobe University and RMIT University, creating a national centre for synthetic diamond R&D supporting quantum computing and sensing.

Raised USD $18 million in additional funding from Breakthrough Victoria, Main Sequence, Investible, Ultratech Capital Partners, MA Growth Ventures, Jelix Ventures, Rampersand, and CM Equity Partners, to expand global operations and improve room-temperature quantum hardware manufacturing.

Awarded a contract by Germany's Cyber Agency (Cyberagentur) in partnership with ParityQC to develop the world's first mobile quantum computer by 2027, the largest-ever research contract awarded by Cyberagentur (valued at approximately €35 million).

Received AUD $13 million equity investment from Australia's National Reconstruction Fund Corporation (NRFC) to establish Australia's first quantum diamond foundry for designing and fabricating quantum diamond devices.

Raised USD $20 million in Series A funding co-led by Main Sequence and In-Q-Tel, with participation from Intervalley Ventures, National Reconstruction Fund Corporation, Breakthrough Victoria, Alium Capital Management, Investible, and Jelix Ventures.

Deployed QB-QDK2.0 at Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Solid State Physics (Fraunhofer IAF) in Freiburg, Germany — the first commercial purchase of a room-temperature quantum accelerator in the European market — a 19-inch rack-mountable NV-center diamond system with integrated NVIDIA GPUs and CPUs.

Deployed a cluster of three Quantum Development Kits (QB-QDK) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory's Advanced Computing Ecosystem testbed in Tennessee — Quantum Brilliance's first US deployment — featuring three parallelized QPUs for a total of 6 qubits, integrated with classical HPC infrastructure for hybrid quantum-classical workflows.

name: NVision Imaging Technologies
short_summary: NVision Imaging Technologies (founded 2015, Ulm, Germany) is a University of Ulm spin-out co-founded by quantum physicists Fedor Jelezko (113-fedor-jelezko), Martin Plenio, Ilai Schwartz, and Alex Retzker. The company applies quantum spin-control technology — originating from NV-center research on diamond surfaces — to produce hyperpolarized carbon-13 metabolic contrast agents for MRI. Its POLARIS platform uses parahydrogen-induced polarization (PHIP) to boost MRI signals by over 10,000x in under three minutes, enabling real-time visualization of tumour metabolism on standard MRI systems. By end-2025, POLARIS Preclinical was deployed at approximately 20 centres including Memorial Sloan Kettering and Technical University of Munich. Having raised USD $120 million total (Series A led by Playground Global, Series B anchored by Abbott with EIB venture loan), NVision rebranded as NVision Quantum Technologies GmbH in May 2026 and announced expansion into photonic quantum computing (PIQC platform) for drug discovery.

differentiators: POLARIS uses parahydrogen-induced polarization (PHIP) to amplify the MRI signal of [1-13C] pyruvate by over 10,000x in under three minutes, enabling real-time metabolic imaging on standard clinical MRI systems without hardware modification

Technology originated from NV-center quantum research at Ulm University (Plenio/Jelezko groups) on polarizing nuclear spins on diamond surfaces, later transferred to liquid-state metabolic contrast agents

POLARIS Preclinical system produces 0.8–2 mL doses at 80–160 mM with a throughput of up to 3 doses/hour, enabling repeat-dosing studies across oncology, cardiology, hepatology, nephrology, and neurology indications
In 2026, NVision expanded into photonic quantum computing (PIQC platform) using organic molecule-based qubits integrated on photonic chips for drug discovery
approach.elevator_pitch: NVision (formerly NVision Imaging Technologies) is a University of Ulm spin-out founded by quantum physicists Martin Plenio and Fedor Jelezko that applies quantum spin-control technology to medical imaging. Its POLARIS platform produces hyperpolarized carbon-13 pyruvate contrast agents via parahydrogen-induced polarization, boosting MRI metabolic signals by over 10,000x to enable real-time cancer metabolic imaging on existing hospital MRI systems.

name: Element Six
short_summary: Element Six (founded 1946, Didcot, UK) is a De Beers Group company and the world's leading manufacturer of synthetic diamond and superhard materials, with over 1,900 employees across the UK, Ireland, Germany, South Africa, and the US. It is the primary global supplier of quantum-grade CVD single-crystal diamond for NV-center qubit research, selling the DNV-B1 and DNV-B14 product lines that provide engineered NV-centre density for quantum sensing, quantum computing, quantum networking, and room-temperature masers. Key quantum partnerships include IonQ (foundry-compatible diamond films for quantum memories and photonic interconnects, announced September 2025), AWS (quantum networking research collaboration), the University of Maryland Quantum Technology Center / Walsworth Group (magnetometry characterisation), and Orbray (wafer-scale 50 mm diamond substrates). Element Six was selected for the DARPA LADDIS and UWBGS defence programs (2023-2024) and made a strategic investment in quantum interconnect startup Lightsynq (acquired by IonQ in June 2025). The company's Global Innovation Centre is located at Harwell, Didcot, Oxfordshire, and its advanced US manufacturing facility is in Gresham, Oregon.

differentiators: Sole industrial-scale manufacturer of quantum-grade CVD single-crystal diamond for NV-center applications, supplying the global research and commercial quantum ecosystem with materials that are not available from any other source at comparable purity and NV-centre density control

DNV product line (DNV-B1 and DNV-B14) provides deliberately engineered, controlled NV-centre densities — DNV-B14 offers more than 10-fold higher NV density than DNV-B1 — enabling researchers to select the optimal trade-off between coherence time and signal strength for their application

Advanced synthetic diamond manufacturing facility in Gresham, Oregon (US) and Global Innovation Centre in Harwell, Didcot (UK) together constitute the world's most capable single-crystal CVD diamond production infrastructure, with substrates up to 50 mm diameter now achievable
Strategic equity investor in quantum-focused startups (Lightsynq, acquired by IonQ June 2025), positioning Element Six at the centre of the emerging diamond quantum networking supply chain
approach.elevator_pitch: Element Six (part of De Beers Group) is the world's leading manufacturer of synthetic diamond and superhard materials, and the primary global supplier of quantum-grade CVD single-crystal diamond for NV-center qubit research and quantum technology applications. Its DNV product line provides engineered diamonds with precisely controlled nitrogen-vacancy centre density for quantum sensing, quantum computing, quantum networking, and room-temperature masers. Element Six also supplies diamond as a critical enabling material to companies such as Quantum Brilliance and research groups at AWS, IonQ, and the University of Maryland.

Ideal starting material for quantum demonstrations, masers, RF detection, gyroscopes, and magnetic sensing. Available in multiple form factors (e.g. 3.0x3.0 mm plates, 0.5 mm thick). Won the 2021 SPIE Prism Award in the quantum category, validated by the Walsworth Group at the University of Maryland Quantum Technology Center.

Uniform NV-centre distribution across the substrate. Launched September 2021.

Achieved breakthrough in chemical vapour deposition (CVD) technology for diamond synthesis, opening new application areas including diamond films and, eventually, quantum-grade substrates.
Changed company name to Element Six, reflecting diversification beyond industrial abrasives into electronic, optical, and advanced materials applications.

Launched DNV-B1™, Element Six's first commercially available general-purpose quantum-grade CVD single-crystal diamond, engineered with controlled NV-centre density for quantum sensing, masers, gyroscopes, and RF detection applications. Won the 2021 SPIE Prism Award in the quantum category.

Launched DNV-B14™, a new quantum-grade CVD diamond providing more than 10-fold higher NV-centre density than DNV-B1, targeting magnetic field devices, RF sensors, solid-state gyroscopes, and room-temperature masers.

Selected as a performer for the US DARPA LADDIS (Large Area Device-quality Diamond Substrates) program, partnered with Raytheon and the University of Bristol, targeting 50 mm diameter single-crystal diamond substrates with dislocation density below 10³ cm⁻² and surface roughness below 0.2 nm.

Announced collaboration with IonQ on quantum-grade synthetic diamond films compatible with standard semiconductor foundries, enabling bonding of diamond onto silicon and silicon nitride substrates and unlocking industrial-scale fabrication of quantum memories and photonic interconnects.

name: Atom Computing
short_summary: Atom Computing (founded 2018, Berkeley CA) builds gate-based quantum computers using nuclear-spin qubits in optically trapped ytterbium-171 atoms. Its AC1000 system — the first to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based platform (1,180 qubits announced October 2023) — features 1,200+ fully-connected physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, single-qubit fidelity >99.9%, and on-premises or cloud (Azure Quantum) deployment. A Microsoft partnership (September 2024) demonstrated 24 entangled logical qubits on record; the companies are co-building the "Magne" system for Denmark. In May 2026, Atom signed a $100 million CHIPS Act Letter of Intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce.

AC1000 available as an on-premises system (~600 sq ft footprint, no cryogenics required) as well as through Azure Quantum cloud access

name: Infleqtion

milestones.claim: ColdQuanta founded in Boulder, CO by Dana Z. Anderson (University of Colorado Boulder / JILA) to commercialise cold-atom and BEC technology developed in his research group; early products were miniaturised cold-atom sources and BEC systems for government and academic customers.

Raised an undisclosed Series A round led by global investors to scale manufacturing of cold-atom systems and pursue quantum computing development; headcount and revenue grew as DoD contracts expanded.

Raised $110 million Series B led by Baidu (joined by global strategic investors) to fund development of the Hilbert quantum computer and Oqtant quantum matter platform; valuation reportedly exceeded $1 billion (unicorn milestone).

Launched Oqtant, a cloud-accessible quantum matter service providing programmable access to an ultracold rubidium Bose–Einstein condensate in an optical lattice, becoming one of the first commercial quantum matter platforms available to external users.
Rebranded from ColdQuanta to Infleqtion, signalling expansion beyond cold-atom hardware into full-stack quantum computing and sensing; headquarters remained in Boulder, CO.

Announced the Hilbert quantum computer — a gate-based system using Rydberg-mediated entangling gates in optically trapped rubidium atoms — as the flagship computing product, with early cloud access offered to partners.
Announced strategic partnership with SandboxAQ (an Alphabet spin-out) to integrate Infleqtion sensing and timing hardware into SandboxAQ navigation and security solutions.

Secured significant DARPA and DoD contracts — including participation in the DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative and multiple DoD-funded sensing programmes — providing non-dilutive government revenue alongside commercial quantum computing activity.
